economics.productivity-explain.0011.all: Training raises workers' skills/knowledge, so they work faster with fewer mistakes, so output per worker at the Leeds factory rises (also may raise motivation).

economics.productivity-mcq-auth.0002.all: Boredom from repeating the same task

economics.productivity-mcq-def.0006.all: Production that uses a high proportion of workers/labour relative to capital

economics.protection-analyse-1.0004.all: Quota limits imports so domestic rice producers gain market share and output; protects jobs and incomes; counters dumping (below cost imports); improves current account; food security; higher prices raise producer revenue.

economics.protection-analyse-2.0001.all: Removal of tariffs means larger foreign firms with economies of scale undercut Gallendra firms; loss of market share, lower profit, closures and job losses; pressure to cut costs; but (one-sided OK).

economics.protection-analyse-3.0001.all: Tariff raises price of imported steel; imports fall; domestic producers gain demand, raise output/price; higher steel prices raise costs for steel-using firms; government revenue; quantity bought overall falls; possible retaliation.

economics.protection-assess-1.0005.all: Benefits: protects domestic producers/jobs, stops dumping, food security, current account. Costs: higher rice prices for consumers (staple, regressive), less choice, inefficiency, retaliation, no quota revenue. Judgement depends on duration and dumping evidence.

economics.protection-assess-2.0004.all: Benefits: access to 709m-consumer market, economies of scale, cheaper imports/inputs, more choice, FDI, competition raises efficiency. Costs: weaker firms close, job losses, trade diversion. Judgement: depends on competitiveness of Eskaria's firms; long-run gains likely.

economics.protection-assess-3.0006.all: Protects jobs: dearer imports shift demand to domestic steel. But: higher costs for steel-using firms (cars, construction) reduce their output/jobs; retaliation hits exporters; inefficiency; may only delay decline. Judgement depends on PED, scale of steel-using industries.

economics.protection-data.0008.b: Larger foreign firms with economies of scale undercut Halvoria firms after tariffs removed; lose market share/profits; closures and unemployment; pressure to cut costs/wages.
economics.protection-data.0008.c: Plan: benefits — access to 425m consumers, economies of scale, cheaper imports and inputs, more choice, FDI, efficiency. Costs — weaker firms close, structural unemployment, trade diversion, loss of tariff revenue. Judgement: depends on competitiveness and time period.

economics.protection-define1.0007.all: A new industry that has not yet grown large enough to benefit from economies of scale and so cannot yet compete with established foreign firms.

economics.protection-define2.0004.all: A group of countries that remove trade barriers between themselves (1) but each keeps its own barriers against non-members (1).

economics.protection-describe.0008.all: A quota is a limit on the quantity of imports, so foreign supply is restricted and domestic producers can sell more / charge higher prices.

economics.protection-diagram.0011.all: Demand for imported tyres shifts left (D1); lower equilibrium price P1 and lower quantity Q1.

economics.protection-evaluate-1.0001.all: Plan: benefits — protects producers and jobs, counters dumping, food security, current account. Costs — higher price of staple food for consumers (hits poor), less choice, inefficiency, retaliation, government gets no revenue (vs tariff). Judgement depends on whether dumping is real, duration.

economics.protection-evaluate-2.0005.all: Plan: benefits — access to 1102m consumers, economies of scale, cheaper imports, choice, FDI, competition. Costs — firms lose to larger rivals, unemployment, trade diversion, loss of tariff revenue. Judgement: short-run costs vs long-run gains.

economics.protection-evaluate-3.0002.all: Plan: protects steel jobs via dearer imports. Against: higher costs for steel-using industries cut their jobs; retaliation hurts exporters; inefficiency; consumers pay more. Judgement depends on PED for imports, relative size of industries, time.

economics.protection-explain.0006.all: Removing tariff lowers the price of imported palm oil, so consumers in Corvana pay less (price could fall up to ~11%), raising real incomes / more choice, and products using palm oil may get cheaper.

economics.protection-mcq-auth.0002.all: raise the price of imported shoes

economics.protection-mcq-def.0004.all: A group of countries that remove trade barriers between themselves but each keeps its own barriers against non-members

economics.protection-state-class.0002.all: Protect infant industries / prevent dumping / protect jobs

economics.redistribution-analyse-1.0001.all: Higher benefits raise incomes of 18% in relative poverty -> better living standards, health, education; low earners have high MPC so spending rises, multiplier; reduces inequality (top 10% get 35%), social cohesion, human capital.

economics.redistribution-analyse-2.0002.all: Sales tax of 17% is regressive: poor spend a larger share of income, so pay higher % of income in tax; flat 12% income tax is proportional, not progressive, so does not reduce inequality; combined system takes larger share from poor.

economics.redistribution-assess-1.0002.all: For: raises revenue to fund benefits/services for 21% in poverty; reduces inequality (top 10% get 41%). Against: disincentive to work, tax avoidance/emigration, limited revenue; alternatives — education, minimum wage, jobs, benefits. Judgement depends on use of revenue.

economics.redistribution-assess-2.0003.all: For: current 20% sales tax regressive, flat 11% income tax; progressive system reduces inequality and raises revenue fairly. Against: disincentives, avoidance, brain drain, admin cost. Judgement depends on rates and use of revenue.

economics.protection-state.0004.problem: Question asks for an example of a trading bloc but the mark scheme lists types of trading bloc (free trade area, customs union, etc.), not named blocs.
economics.protection-state.0004.fix: Award 1 mark for any named trading bloc, e.g. EU, ASEAN, USMCA, Mercosur, ECOWAS; or reword the question to 'State one type of trading bloc'.
